2816: #### 1. General description
2817: 
2818: This Part of the specification provides an overview of the Bluetooth system architecture, communication topologies, and data transport features. The text in this Part of the specification is intended to provide an introduction to Bluetooth and does not cover every detail or every corner case. In case of discrepancy with other parts of this specification, the other text is to be relied on.
2819: 
2820: Bluetooth wireless technology is a short-range communications system intended to replace the cable(s) connecting portable and/or fixed electronic devices. The key features of Bluetooth wireless technology are robustness, low power consumption, and low cost. Many features of the specification are optional, allowing product differentiation.
2821: 
2822: There are two forms of Bluetooth wireless technology systems: Basic Rate (BR) and Low Energy (LE). Both systems include device discovery, connection establishment and connection mechanisms. The Basic Rate system includes an optional Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) extension. The Basic Rate system offers synchronous and asynchronous connections with data rates of 721.2 kb/s for Basic Rate and 2.1 Mb/s for Enhanced Data Rate. The LE system includes features designed to enable products that require lower current consumption, lower complexity and lower cost than BR/EDR. The LE system is also designed for use cases and applications with lower data rates and has lower duty cycles. The LE system includes an optional 2 Mb/s physical layer data rate and also offers isochronous data transfer in a connection-oriented and connectionless mechanism that uses the isochronous transports. The LE system also includes the optional modulation of tones used to convey information useful for distance estimation. Depending on the use case or application, one system including any optional parts may be more optimal than the other. 
2823: 
2824: Devices implementing both systems can communicate with other devices implementing both systems as well as devices implementing either system. Some profiles and use cases will be supported by only one of the systems. Therefore, devices implementing both systems have the ability to support the most use cases.
2825: 
2826: The Bluetooth core system consists of a Host and one or more Controllers. A Host is a logical entity defined as all of the layers below the non-core profiles and above the Host Controller interface (HCI). A Controller is a logical entity defined as all of the layers below HCI. An implementation of the Host and Controller may contain the respective parts of the HCI.
2827: 
2828: An implementation of the Bluetooth Core has only one Controller which may be one of the following configurations:
2829: 
2830: -   a BR/EDR Controller including the Radio, Baseband, Link Manager and optionally HCI.
2831:     
2832: -   an LE Controller including the LE PHY, Link Layer and optionally HCI.
2833:     
2834: -   a combined BR/EDR Controller portion and LE Controller portion (as identified in the previous two bullets) into a single Controller.
2835:

2844: ##### 1.1. Overview of BR/EDR operation
2845: 
2846: The Basic Rate / Enhanced Data Rate (BR/EDR) radio (physical layer or PHY) operates in the unlicensed ISM band at 2.4 GHz. The system employs a frequency hopping transceiver to combat interference and fading and provides many FHSS carriers. Basic Rate radio operation uses a shaped, binary frequency modulation to minimize transceiver complexity. The symbol rate is 1 megasymbol per second (Msym/s) supporting the bit rate of 1 megabit per second (Mb/s) or, with Enhanced Data Rate, a gross air bit rate of 2 Mb/s or 3 Mb/s. These modes are known as Basic Rate and Enhanced Data Rate respectively.
2847: 
2848: During typical operation a physical radio channel is shared by a group of devices that are synchronized to a common clock and frequency hopping pattern. One device provides the synchronization reference and is known as the Central. All other devices synchronized to a Central’s clock and frequency hopping pattern are known as Peripherals. A group of devices synchronized in this fashion form a piconet. This is the fundamental form of communication in the Bluetooth BR/EDR wireless technology.
2849: 
2850: Devices in a piconet use a specific frequency hopping pattern, which is algorithmically determined by certain fields in the Bluetooth address and clock of the Central. The basic hopping pattern is a pseudo-random ordering of the 79 frequencies, separated by 1 MHz, in the ISM band. The hopping pattern can be adapted – on a per-Peripheral basis – to omit a portion of the frequencies that are used by interfering devices. The adaptive hopping technique improves Bluetooth co-existence with static (non-hopping) ISM systems when they are co-located.
2851: 
2852: The physical channel is sub-divided into time units known as slots. Data is transmitted between Bluetooth devices in packets that are positioned in these slots. When circumstances permit, a number of consecutive slots may be allocated to a single packet. Frequency hopping may take place between the transmission or reception of packets. Bluetooth technology provides the effect of full duplex transmission through the use of a Time-Division Duplex (TDD) scheme.
2853: 
2854: Above the physical channel there is a layering of links and channels and associated control protocols. The hierarchy of channels and links from the physical channel upwards is physical channel, physical link, logical transport, logical link and L2CAP channel. These are discussed in more detail in [Section 3.3](architecture.html#UUID-02099e77-5773-8804-f35e-2f1b57984e6a "3.3 Physical channels") to [Section 3.6](architecture.html#UUID-436dd8c4-f88a-160d-1e66-a065255f82cf "3.6 L2CAP channels") but are introduced here to aid the understanding of the remainder of this section.
2855: 
2856: Typically within a physical channel, a physical link is formed between a Central and one or more Peripherals. Exceptions to this include Inquiry scan and Page scan physical channels, which have no associated physical link. The physical link provides bidirectional packet transport between the Central and Peripherals, except in the case of a Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link. In that case, the physical link provides a unidirectional packet transport from the Central to a potentially unlimited number of Peripherals. Since a physical channel could include multiple Peripherals, there are restrictions on which devices may form a physical link. There is a physical link between each Peripheral and the Central. Physical links are not formed directly between the Peripherals in a piconet.
2857: 
2858: The physical link is used as a transport for one or more logical links that support unicast synchronous, asynchronous and isochronous traffic, and broadcast traffic. Traffic on logical links is multiplexed onto the physical link by occupying slots assigned by a scheduling function in the resource manager.
2859: 
2860: A control protocol for the baseband and physical layers is carried over logical links in addition to user data. This is the Link Manager protocol (LMP). Devices that are active in a piconet have a default asynchronous connection-oriented logical transport that is used to transport the LMP protocol signaling. For historical reasons this is known as the ACL logical transport. With the exception of Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast devices, the primary ACL logical transport is the one that is created whenever a device joins a piconet. Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast devices may join the piconet purely to listen to Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast packets. In that case, a Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast logical transport is created (also called a CPB logical transport) and no ACL logical transport is required. For all devices, additional logical transports may be created to transport synchronous data streams when required.
2861: 
2862: The Link Manager function uses LMP to control the operation of devices in the piconet and provide services to manage the lower architectural layers (radio and baseband). The LMP protocol is carried on the primary ACL and Active Peripheral Broadcast logical transports.
2863: 
2864: Above the baseband the L2CAP layer provides a channel-based abstraction to applications and services. It carries out segmentation and reassembly of application data and multiplexing and de-multiplexing of multiple channels over a shared logical link. L2CAP has a protocol control channel that is carried over the default ACL logical transport. Application data submitted to the L2CAP protocol may be carried on any logical link that supports the L2CAP protocol.
2865: 
2866: ##### 1.2. Overview of Bluetooth Low Energy operation
2867: 
2868: Like the BR/EDR radio, the LE radio operates in the unlicensed 2.4 GHz ISM band. The LE system employs a frequency hopping transceiver to combat interference and fading and provides many FHSS carriers. LE radio operation uses a shaped, binary frequency modulation, and optional amplitude shift keying modulation to minimize transceiver complexity. LE uses terminology that differs from BR/EDR to describe supported PHYs with regards to differences in modulation, coding that may be applied, and the resulting data rates. The mandatory symbol rate is 1 megasymbol per second (Msym/s), where 1 symbol represents 1 bit therefore supporting a bit rate of 1 megabit per second (Mb/s), which is referred to as the LE 1M PHY. The 1 Msym/s symbol rate may support error correction coding, which is referred to as the LE Coded PHY. This may use either of two coding schemes: S=2, where 2 symbols represent 1 bit therefore supporting a bit rate of 500 kb/s, and S=8, where 8 symbols represent 1 bit therefore supporting a bit rate of 125 kb/s. A symbol rate of 2 Msym/s may be supported, with a bit rate of 2 Mb/s, which is referred to as the LE 2M PHY, when using a bandwidth-symbol time product (BT) of 0.5. An additional optional symbol rate at 2 Msym/s using a BT of 2.0 is also supported when used for the purpose of distance estimation, which is referred to as the LE 2M 2BT PHY. The 2 Msym/s symbol rate supports uncoded data only. LE 1M, LE 2M, and 2M 2BT are collectively referred to as the LE Uncoded PHYs. [Section 3.2.2](architecture.html#UUID-68615d2c-776f-f78d-1f4f-5b514754f641 "3.2.2 LE generic packet structure") describes this terminology in more detail.
2869: 
2870: The amplitude shift keying modulation scheme is employed to modulate tones for the purpose of gathering information for distance estimation. [Section 3.2.3](architecture.html#UUID-f17d361b-e999-4033-9685-5e349b217a60 "3.2.3 LE Channel Sounding generic packet structure and signaling format") describes amplitude shift keying in more detail. 
2871: 
2872: LE employs two multiple access schemes: Frequency division multiple access (FDMA) and time division multiple access (TDMA). A TDMA-based polling scheme is used in which one device transmits a packet at a predetermined time and a corresponding device responds with a packet after a predetermined interval. 
2873: 
2874: For the purposes of data transfer, 40 physical channels, separated by 2 MHz, are used in the FDMA scheme. Three are used as primary advertising channels and 37 are used as general-purpose channels (including as secondary advertising channels). 
2875: 
2876: For the purpose of distance estimation, 72 physical channels, separated by 1 MHz, are used in the FDMA scheme. 
2877: 
2878: The physical channel is sub-divided into time units known as events. Data is transmitted between LE devices in packets that are positioned in these events. The following types of events exist: Advertising, Extended Advertising, Periodic Advertising, Connection, Isochronous events (which are partitioned into BIS, BIG, CIS, and CIG events), and Channel Sounding events. 
2879: 
2880: Devices that transmit advertising packets on the advertising PHY channels are referred to as advertisers. Devices that receive advertising packets on the advertising physical channels without the intention to connect to the advertising device are referred to as scanners. Transmissions on the advertising PHY channels occur in advertising events. At the start of each advertising event, the advertiser sends an advertising packet corresponding to the advertising event type. Depending on the type of advertising packet, the scanner may make a request to the advertiser on the same advertising PHY channel which may be followed by a response from the advertiser on the same advertising PHY channel. The advertising PHY channel changes on the next advertising packet sent by the advertiser in the same advertising event. The advertiser may end the advertising event at any time during the event. Each advertising packet in an advertising event uses a different advertising PHY channel. Each advertising event may use a different order for the advertising PHY channels.
2881: 
2882: ![Advertising events](../image/img-d3fceb110ae0ea3ad3157367b9d42e29.png)
2883: 
2884: Figure 1.2: Advertising events
2885: 
2886:   
2887:   
2888: 
2889: LE devices may fulfill the entire communication in the case of unidirectional or broadcast communication between two or more devices using advertising events. LE devices may also use advertising events to establish bi-directional connections with another device and to establish asynchronous or isochronous periodic broadcasts. Asynchronous periodic broadcasts may allow the advertiser to receive responses from one or more devices. These additional activities make use of the general purpose channels in various ways.
2890: 
2891: Devices that need to form an ACL connection to another device listen for connectable advertising packets. Such devices are referred to as initiators. If the advertiser is using a connectable advertising event, an initiator may make a connection request using the same advertising PHY channel on which it received the connectable advertising packet. The advertising event is ended and connection events begin if the advertiser receives and accepts the request for a connection be initiated. Once a connection is established, the initiator becomes the Central in what is referred to as a piconet and the advertising device becomes the Peripheral. Connection events are used to send data packets between the Central and Peripherals. In connection events, channel hopping occurs at the start of each connection event. Within a connection event, the Central and Peripheral alternate sending data packets using the same data PHY channel. The Central initiates the beginning of each connection event and can end each connection event at any time.
2892: 
2893: ![Connection events](../image/img-307f1981ef5d877f350327f5ff930668.png)
2894: 
2895: Figure 1.3: Connection events
2896: 
2897:   
2898:   
2899: 
2900: Devices in a piconet use a specific frequency hopping pattern, which is algorithmically determined by a field contained in the connection request sent by an initiating device. The hopping pattern used on the LE data channel is a pseudo-random ordering of the 37 frequencies in the ISM band. The hopping pattern used in a Channel Sounding procedure is a pseudo-random ordering of 72 frequencies in the ISM band. The hopping pattern can be adapted to omit a portion of the frequencies that are used by interfering devices. The adaptive hopping technique improves Bluetooth co-existence with static (non-hopping) ISM systems when these systems are co-located and have access to information about the local radio environment. A Peripheral can classify frequencies as good and bad and provide that information to the Central. The Central can take this information into consideration while adapting the hopping pattern. 
2901: 
2902: Using an ACL connection, a Central can establish one or more isochronous connections that use the isochronous physical channel. An isochronous connection is used to transfer isochronous data between the Central and a Peripheral by using a logical transport, which is referred to as a Connected Isochronous Stream (CIS). A CIS consists of CIS events that occur at regular intervals (designated ISO\_Interval). Every CIS event consists of one or more subevents. In each subevent, the Central transmits once and the Peripheral responds. If the Central and Peripheral have completed transferring the scheduled isochronous data in a CIS event, all remaining subevents in that event will have no radio transmissions and the event is closed. Each subevent uses a PHY channel which is determined by using the channel selection algorithm. The PHY channel that is used for a subevent is marked as ISO Ch(eventcount, subeventcount), as shown in [Figure 1.4](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4553496317956833541868208267 "Figure 1.4: CIS events and subevents").
2903: 
2904: ![CIS events and subevents](../image/img-f6feee2e045be4b33509ab7b5566f149.png)
2905: 
2906: Figure 1.4: CIS events and subevents
2907: 
2908:   
2909:   
2910: 
2911: A device can use an isochronous physical channel to broadcast isochronous data by using isochronous connectionless logical transports. An isochronous connectionless logical transport is referred to as a Broadcast Isochronous Stream (BIS). A BIS consists of BIS events that occur at regular intervals (designated ISO\_Interval). Every BIS event consists of one or more subevents. In every subevent, a broadcasting device transmits an isochronous data packet. Each subevent uses a PHY channel that is determined using the channel selection algorithm.
2912: 
2913: A device can transmit several BISes with synchronized timing; this is referred to as a Broadcast Isochronous Group (BIG). The various BIS events together form a BIG event. The device can also use the isochronous physical channel to broadcast control information in a Control subevent, which is transmitted at the end of all subevents for a BIG, as shown in [Figure 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent").
2914: 
2915: A device that transmits BIG events also transmits periodic advertisement events that contain synchronization information of the BIG. A device that is scanning can synchronize to those periodic advertising events and receive the synchronization information. Using this synchronization information, the device can synchronize to one or more BISes in the BIG and receive the isochronous data. [Figure 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent") shows two BIG events: one with and one without a Control subevent. Each subevent uses a PHY channel marked as ISO Ch(eventcount, subeventcount), as shown in [Figure 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent").

2924: Devices can use the LE Channel Sounding physical link to exchange information that can later be used for distance estimation calculations. A Channel Sounding procedure (and hence, the first Channel Sounding event within that procedure) is started at an offset from an ACL connection event anchor point. A Channel Sounding procedure exists only for a limited duration, and consists of Channel Sounding events, subevents, and steps. Channel Sounding events may contain one or more subevents. Channel Sounding subevents contain two or more Channel Sounding steps. Channel Sounding steps contain bilateral exchanges between the two Channel Sounding peers known as the initiator and reflector. The Channel Sounding initiator transmits first in each step, followed by one or more transmissions from the Channel Sounding reflector. These transmissions may be a packet-based GFSK-modulated exchange or a tone-based, amplitude shift keying modulated exchange, or both. 
2925: 
2926: The general structure of Channel Sounding events and subevents is shown in [Figure 1.6](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4589043074160033833279531065 "Figure 1.6: Channel Sounding events and subevents ").

2929: 
2930: Figure 1.6: Channel Sounding events and subevents

2933:   
2934: 
2935: Each exchange within a Channel Sounding step contains information that can be measured. These measurements can be further processed to produce a distance estimate. The step content is discussed in more detail in [\[Vol 6\] Part H, Section 4.3](../low-energy-controller/channel-sounding.html#UUID-723b65d3-d0db-3b20-2d99-3acc7477d13f "4.3 Channel Sounding steps"). These exchanges also carry security-related information that may assist in the detection of an external attacker who is attempting to indirectly manipulate the measured results, which could in turn affect the distance estimate. The Channel Sounding step exchanges use a PHY channel that is determined using a channel selection algorithm. For Channel Sounding, this channel selection algorithm, as well as other security-related information, is seeded using a Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG). The security key material for this DRBG is known only by the respective initiator and reflector devices. 
2936: 
2937: Above the physical channel there are concepts of links, channels and associated control protocols. The hierarchy is physical channel, physical link, logical transport, logical link, and L2CAP channel. These are discussed in more detail in [Section 3.3](architecture.html#UUID-02099e77-5773-8804-f35e-2f1b57984e6a "3.3 Physical channels") to [Section 3.6](architecture.html#UUID-436dd8c4-f88a-160d-1e66-a065255f82cf "3.6 L2CAP channels") but are introduced here to aid the understanding of the remainder of this section.
2938: 
2939: Within a physical channel, a physical link is formed between devices. The active physical link provides bidirectional packet transport between the Central and Peripherals. Centrals may have physical links to more than one Peripheral at a time and Peripherals may have physical links to more than one Central at a time. A device may be Central and Peripheral in different piconets at the same time. Role changes between a Central and Peripheral are not supported. The advertising and periodic physical links provide a unidirectional packet transport from the advertiser to a potentially unlimited number of scanners or initiators.
2940: 
2941: The physical link is used as a transport for one or more logical links that support asynchronous traffic. Traffic on logical links is multiplexed onto the physical link assigned by a scheduling function in the resource manager.
2942: 
2943: A control protocol for the link and physical layers is carried over logical links in addition to user data. This is the Link Layer protocol (LL). Devices that are active in a piconet have a default LE asynchronous connection logical transport (LE ACL) that is used to transport the LL protocol signaling. The default LE ACL is the one that is created whenever a piconet is created.
2944: 
2945: The Link Layer function uses the LL protocol to control the operation of devices in the piconet and provide services to manage the lower architectural layers (PHY and LL).
2946: 
2947: Overall, a piconet consists of one ACL logical transport over the active physical link plus zero or more CIS logical transports over the isochronous physical link(s). In addition, zero or more transitory Channel Sounding procedures may exist over the Channel Sounding physical link. 
2948: 
2949: Just as in BR/EDR, above the Link Layer the L2CAP layer provides a channel-based abstraction to applications and services. It carries out fragmentation and de-fragmentation of application data and multiplexing and de-multiplexing of multiple channels over a shared logical link. L2CAP has a protocol control channel that is carried over the primary ACL logical transport.
2950: 
2951: In addition to L2CAP, LE provides two additional protocol layers that reside on top of L2CAP. The Security Manager protocol (SMP) uses a fixed L2CAP channel to implement the security functions between devices. The other is the Attribute Protocol (ATT) that provides a method to communicate small amounts of data over a fixed L2CAP channel. The Attribute Protocol is also used by devices to determine the services and capabilities of other devices. The Attribute Protocol may also be used over BR/EDR.
2952: 
2953: The LE radio provides a means for detecting the relative direction of another LE radio by using the Angle of Arrival (AoA) or Angle of Departure (AoD) method.

#### 1. 一般描述

本部分规范提供了蓝牙系统架构、通信拓扑和数据传输特性的概述。本部分规范中的文本旨在介绍蓝牙，并未涵盖每个细节或每种边界情况。若本部分与其他部分存在不一致之处，应以其他文本为准。

蓝牙无线技术是一种短距离通信系统，旨在取代连接便携和/或固定电子设备的线缆。蓝牙无线技术的关键特性是健壮性、低功耗和低成本。本规范中的许多特性是可选的，从而允许产品差异化。

蓝牙无线技术系统有两种形式：基本速率（BR）和低功耗（LE）。两种系统都包括设备发现、连接建立和连接机制。基本速率系统包括可选的增强数据速率（EDR）扩展。基本速率系统提供同步和异步连接，基本速率的数据速率为 721.2 kb/s，增强数据速率的数据速率为 2.1 Mb/s。LE 系统包含的特性旨在使产品能够实现比 BR/EDR 更低的电流消耗、更低的复杂度和更低的成本。LE 系统也适用于具有较低数据速率和较低占空比的使用场景和应用。LE 系统包括可选的 2 Mb/s 物理层数据速率，并且还通过使用等时传输的面向连接和无连接机制提供等时数据传输。LE 系统还包括用于传输对距离估计有用的信息的音调的可选调制。根据使用场景或应用的不同，包含任何可选部分的某一系统可能比另一系统更为优化。

实现两种系统的设备可以与实现两种系统的其他设备以及实现任一系统的设备进行通信。某些配置文件和使用场景仅由其中一种系统支持。因此，实现两种系统的设备能够支持最多的使用场景。

蓝牙核心系统由一个主机和一个或多个控制器组成。主机是一个逻辑实体，定义为非核心配置文件以下、主机控制器接口（HCI）以上的所有层。控制器是一个逻辑实体，定义为 HCI 以下的所有层。主机和控制器的实现可以包含 HCI 的相应部分。

蓝牙核心的实现只有一个控制器，可以是以下配置之一：

-   包含射频、基带、链路管理器以及可选 HCI 的 BR/EDR 控制器。
    
-   包含 LE PHY、链路层以及可选 HCI 的 LE 控制器。
    
-   将 BR/EDR 控制器部分和 LE 控制器部分（如前两项所述）合并为单个控制器的组合控制器。
    

![蓝牙主机与控制器组合：（从左到右）：仅 LE 控制器、仅 BR/EDR 控制器和 BR/EDR/LE 控制器](../image/img-973ab4b7c07241bdb0d1c49d5149f9d0.png)

图 1.1：蓝牙主机与控制器组合：（从左到右）：仅 LE 控制器、仅 BR/EDR 控制器和 BR/EDR/LE 控制器

  
  
  

##### 1.1. BR/EDR 操作概述

基本速率/增强数据速率（BR/EDR）射频（物理层或 PHY）工作在 2.4 GHz 的免许可 ISM 频段。系统采用跳频收发器来对抗干扰和衰落，并提供许多跳频扩频（FHSS）载波。基本速率射频操作使用成形的二进制频率调制，以最小化收发器的复杂度。符号速率为每秒 1 兆符号（Msym/s），支持 1 兆比特每秒（Mb/s）的比特速率，或在增强数据速率下支持 2 Mb/s 或 3 Mb/s 的总空中比特速率。这些模式分别被称为基本速率和增强数据速率。

在典型操作期间，一个物理射频信道由一组同步到公共时钟和跳频图案的设备共享。其中一台设备提供同步参考，被称为中心设备（Central）。所有同步到中心设备时钟和跳频图案的其他设备被称为外围设备（Peripheral）。以这种方式同步的一组设备构成一个微微网（piconet）。这是蓝牙 BR/EDR 无线技术的基本通信形式。

微微网中的设备使用特定的跳频图案，该图案由中心设备的蓝牙地址和时钟中的某些字段通过算法确定。基本跳频图案是 ISM 频段中 79 个间隔 1 MHz 的频率的伪随机排序。跳频图案可以逐个外围设备地进行调整，以省略被干扰设备使用的部分频率。当自适应跳频技术与静态（非跳频）ISM 系统共处一地时，该技术可改善蓝牙与这些系统的共存性。

物理信道被细分为称为时隙的时间单位。数据以分组的形式在蓝牙设备之间传输，这些分组被定位在这些时隙中。在条件允许的情况下，可以将若干连续时隙分配给单个分组。跳频可以在分组的传输或接收之间发生。蓝牙技术通过使用时分双工（TDD）方案提供全双工传输的效果。

在物理信道之上是链路和信道以及相关控制协议的分层结构。从物理信道向上的信道和链路层次为：物理信道、物理链路、逻辑传输、逻辑链路和 L2CAP 信道。这些在 [3.3 节](architecture.html#UUID-02099e77-5773-8804-f35e-2f1b57984e6a "3.3 Physical channels")到 [3.6 节](architecture.html#UUID-436dd8c4-f88a-160d-1e66-a065255f82cf "3.6 L2CAP channels")中有更详细的讨论，但此处先作介绍以帮助理解本节的其余部分。

通常在物理信道内，物理链路在中心设备与一个或多个外围设备之间形成。此规则的例外包括查询扫描和寻呼扫描物理信道，它们没有关联的物理链路。物理链路在中心设备与外围设备之间提供双向分组传输，但在无连接外围广播物理链路的情况下除外。在那种情况下，物理链路提供从中心设备到可能无限数量的外围设备的单向分组传输。由于一个物理信道可能包含多个外围设备，因此对哪些设备可以形成物理链路存在限制。每个外围设备与中心设备之间存在一条物理链路。微微网中的外围设备之间不直接形成物理链路。

物理链路用作一条或多条逻辑链路的传输载体，这些逻辑链路支持单播同步、异步和等时业务以及广播业务。逻辑链路上的业务通过占用资源管理器中调度函数分配的时隙被复用到物理链路上。

除了用户数据之外，基带和物理层的控制协议也通过逻辑链路承载。这就是链路管理器协议（LMP）。在微微网中处于活动状态的设备具有默认的面向连接的异步逻辑传输，用于传输 LMP 协议信令。由于历史原因，这被称为 ACL 逻辑传输。除无连接外围广播设备外，主 ACL 逻辑传输是在设备加入微微网时创建的逻辑传输。无连接外围广播设备加入微微网可能纯粹是为了监听无连接外围广播分组。在这种情况下，会创建一个无连接外围广播逻辑传输（也称为 CPB 逻辑传输），而无需 ACL 逻辑传输。对于所有设备，在需要时可以创建额外的逻辑传输来传输同步数据流。

链路管理器功能使用 LMP 来控制微微网中设备的操作，并提供管理较低架构层（射频和基带）的服务。LMP 协议在主 ACL 和活动外围广播逻辑传输上承载。

在基带之上，L2CAP 层向应用和服务提供基于信道的抽象。它执行应用数据的分段和重组，以及在共享逻辑链路上对多个信道进行复用和分用。L2CAP 具有一个协议控制信道，在默认 ACL 逻辑传输上承载。提交给 L2CAP 协议的应用数据可以在任何支持 L2CAP 协议的逻辑链路上承载。

##### 1.2. 蓝牙低功耗操作概述

与 BR/EDR 射频一样，LE 射频工作在免许可的 2.4 GHz ISM 频段。LE 系统采用跳频收发器来对抗干扰和衰落，并提供许多跳频扩频（FHSS）载波。LE 射频操作使用成形的二进制频率调制以及可选的幅移键控调制，以最小化收发器的复杂度。LE 使用与 BR/EDR 不同的术语来描述所支持的 PHY，这些术语涉及调制、可能应用的编码以及由此产生的数据速率方面的差异。强制符号速率为每秒 1 兆符号（Msym/s），其中 1 个符号表示 1 个比特，因此支持 1 兆比特每秒（Mb/s）的比特速率，这被称为 LE 1M PHY。1 Msym/s 的符号速率可以支持纠错编码，这被称为 LE Coded PHY。这可以使用两种编码方案之一：S=2，其中 2 个符号表示 1 个比特，因此支持 500 kb/s 的比特速率；以及 S=8，其中 8 个符号表示 1 个比特，因此支持 125 kb/s 的比特速率。当使用带宽-符号时间乘积（BT）为 0.5 时，可以支持 2 Msym/s 的符号速率，比特速率为 2 Mb/s，这被称为 LE 2M PHY。当用于距离估计目的时，还支持使用 BT 为 2.0 的 2 Msym/s 的额外可选符号速率，这被称为 LE 2M 2BT PHY。2 Msym/s 的符号速率仅支持未编码数据。LE 1M、LE 2M 和 2M 2BT 统称为 LE 未编码 PHY。[3.2.2 节](architecture.html#UUID-68615d2c-776f-f78d-1f4f-5b514754f641 "3.2.2 LE generic packet structure")更详细地描述了此术语。

采用幅移键控调制方案来调制音调，以收集用于距离估计的信息。[3.2.3 节](architecture.html#UUID-f17d361b-e999-4033-9685-5e349b217a60 "3.2.3 LE Channel Sounding generic packet structure and signaling format")更详细地描述了幅移键控。

LE 采用两种多址接入方案：频分多址（FDMA）和时分多址（TDMA）。使用基于 TDMA 的轮询方案，其中一台设备在预定时间发送分组，对应的设备在预定间隔后以分组响应。

为了进行数据传输，在 FDMA 方案中使用 40 个间隔 2 MHz 的物理信道。其中三个用作主广播信道，37 个用作通用信道（包括作为次级广播信道）。

为了进行距离估计，在 FDMA 方案中使用 72 个间隔 1 MHz 的物理信道。

物理信道被细分为称为事件的时间单位。数据以分组的形式在 LE 设备之间传输，这些分组被定位在这些事件中。存在以下类型的事件：广播、扩展广播、周期性广播、连接、等时事件（分为 BIS、BIG、CIS 和 CIG 事件）以及信道探测事件。

在广播 PHY 信道上发送广播分组的设备被称为广播者。在广播物理信道上接收广播分组且无意与广播设备建立连接的设备被称为扫描者。在广播 PHY 信道上的传输发生在广播（事件）中。在每个广播事件开始时，广播者发送与广播事件类型相对应的广播分组。根据广播分组的类型，扫描者可以在同一广播 PHY 信道上向广播者发出请求，随后广播者可以在同一广播 PHY 信道上进行响应。广播 PHY 信道在广播者在同一广播事件中发送下一个广播分组时发生变化。广播者可以在事件期间的任何时间结束广播事件。一个广播事件中的每个广播分组使用不同的广播 PHY 信道。每个广播事件可以使用不同的广播 PHY 信道顺序。

![广播事件](../image/img-d3fceb110ae0ea3ad3157367b9d42e29.png)

图 1.2：广播事件

  
  
  

在两个或多个设备之间的单向或广播通信的情况下，LE 设备可以仅通过广播事件完成全部通信。LE 设备还可以使用广播事件与另一设备建立双向连接，并建立异步或等时周期性广播。异步周期性广播可以允许广播者从一个或多个设备接收响应。这些附加活动以各种方式使用通用信道。

需要与另一设备形成 ACL 连接的设备监听可连接广播分组。此类设备被称为发起者。如果广播者正在使用可连接广播事件，则发起者可以在其接收到可连接广播分组的同一广播 PHY 信道上发出连接请求。如果广播者接收并接受启动连接的请求，则广播事件结束，连接事件开始。一旦连接建立，发起者就成为所谓的微微网中的中心设备，广播设备成为外围设备。连接事件用于在中心设备与外围设备之间发送数据分组。在连接事件中，在每个连接事件开始时发生跳频。在连接事件内，中心设备和外围设备使用相同的数据 PHY 信道交替发送数据分组。中心设备发起每个连接事件的开始，并可以在任何时间结束每个连接事件。

![连接事件](../image/img-307f1981ef5d877f350327f5ff930668.png)

图 1.3：连接事件

  
  
  

微微网中的设备使用特定的跳频图案，该图案由发起设备发送的连接请求中包含的字段通过算法确定。LE 数据信道上使用的跳频图案是 ISM 频段中 37 个频率的伪随机排序。信道探测过程中使用的跳频图案是 ISM 频段中 72 个频率的伪随机排序。跳频图案可以进行调整，以省略被干扰设备使用的部分频率。当这些系统共处一地并能够获得有关本地射频环境的信息时，自适应跳频技术可改善蓝牙与静态（非跳频）ISM 系统的共存性。外围设备可以将频率分类为好和坏，并将该信息提供给中心设备。中心设备在调整跳频图案时可以考虑此信息。

使用 ACL 连接，中心设备可以建立一条或多条使用等时物理信道的等时连接。等时连接用于通过称为连接等时流（CIS）的逻辑传输在中心设备与外围设备之间传输等时数据。CIS 由以规则间隔（ designated ISO_Interval）发生的 CIS 事件组成。每个 CIS 事件由一个或多个子事件组成。在每个子事件中，中心设备发送一次，外围设备响应一次。如果中心设备和外围设备已经在某个 CIS 事件中完成了计划等时数据的传输，则该事件中所有剩余子事件将没有射频传输，该事件被关闭。每个子事件使用通过信道选择算法确定的 PHY 信道。用于子事件的 PHY 信道被标记为 ISO Ch(eventcount, subeventcount)，如 [图 1.4](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4553496317956833541868208267 "Figure 1.4: CIS events and subevents")所示。

![CIS 事件与子事件](../image/img-f6feee2e045be4b33509ab7b5566f149.png)

图 1.4：CIS 事件与子事件

  
  
  

设备可以使用等时物理信道通过等时无连接逻辑传输来广播等时数据。等时无连接逻辑传输被称为广播等时流（BIS）。BIS 由以规则间隔（ designated ISO_Interval）发生的 BIS 事件组成。每个 BIS 事件由一个或多个子事件组成。在每个子事件中，广播设备发送一个等时数据分组。每个子事件使用通过信道选择算法确定的 PHY 信道。

设备可以以同步时序发送若干 BIS；这被称为广播等时组（BIG）。各 BIS 事件共同构成一个 BIG 事件。设备还可以使用等时物理信道在控制子事件中广播控制信息，该控制子事件在 BIG 的所有子事件结束时发送，如 [图 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent")所示。

发送 BIG 事件的设备还发送包含 BIG 同步信息的周期性广播事件。正在扫描的设备可以同步到那些周期性广播事件并接收同步信息。使用此同步信息，该设备可以同步到 BIG 中的一个或多个 BIS 并接收等时数据。[图 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent")显示了两个 BIG 事件：一个带有控制子事件，一个不带。每个子事件使用标记为 ISO Ch(eventcount, subeventcount)的 PHY 信道，如 [图 1.5](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4568345853323233541870155302 "Figure 1.5: BIG and BIS events, BIS subevents, and Control subevent")所示。

![BIG 与 BIS 事件、BIS 子事件和控制子事件](../image/img-aacb064c9298b8f55396dd5a3cc85fcb.png)

图 1.5：BIG 与 BIS 事件、BIS 子事件和控制子事件

  
  
  

设备可以使用 LE 信道探测物理链路交换信息，这些信息随后可用于距离估计计算。信道探测（CS）过程（因此也包括该过程中的第一个信道探测事件）从 ACL 连接事件锚点偏移开始。信道探测过程仅存在有限的持续时间，并由信道探测事件、子事件和步骤组成。信道探测事件可以包含一个或多个子事件。信道探测子事件包含两个或多个信道探测步骤。信道探测步骤包含两个信道探测对端之间（即发起者和反射者）的双向交换。信道探测发起者在每个步骤中首先发送，随后是信道探测反射者的一次或多次发送。这些发送可以是基于分组的高斯频移键控（GFSK）调制交换、基于音调的幅移键控调制交换，或两者兼有。

信道探测事件和子事件的一般结构如 [图 1.6](architecture.html#UUID-3ca385af-187d-8221-1114-504a7b3c6091_figure-idm4589043074160033833279531065 "Figure 1.6: Channel Sounding events and subevents ")所示。

![信道探测事件与子事件 ](../image/img-5ecbd8514f958788212c4a52e7f2d38e.png)

图 1.6：信道探测事件与子事件 

  
  
  

信道探测步骤中的每次交换包含可被测量的信息。这些测量可以经过进一步处理以产生距离估计。步骤内容在 [\[卷 6\] H 部分，4.3 节](../low-energy-controller/channel-sounding.html#UUID-723b65d3-d0db-3b20-2d99-3acc7477d13f "4.3 Channel Sounding steps")中有更详细的讨论。这些交换还携带与安全相关的信息，可有助于检测试图间接操纵测量结果的外部攻击者，这反过来可能影响距离估计。信道探测步骤交换使用通过信道选择算法确定的 PHY 信道。对于信道探测，此信道选择算法以及其他与安全相关的信息使用确定性随机比特生成器（DRBG）进行种子化。此 DRBG 的安全密钥材料仅由相应的发起者和反射者设备所知。

在物理信道之上存在链路、信道和相关控制协议的概念。层次结构为物理信道、物理链路、逻辑传输、逻辑链路和 L2CAP 信道。这些在 [3.3 节](architecture.html#UUID-02099e77-5773-8804-f35e-2f1b57984e6a "3.3 Physical channels")到 [3.6 节](architecture.html#UUID-436dd8c4-f88a-160d-1e66-a065255f82cf "3.6 L2CAP channels")中有更详细的讨论，但此处先作介绍以帮助理解本节的其余部分。

在物理信道内，设备之间形成物理链路。活动物理链路在中心设备与外围设备之间提供双向分组传输。中心设备可以同时具有与多个外围设备的物理链路，外围设备也可以同时具有与多个中心设备的物理链路。一个设备可以同时在不同微微网中担任中心设备和外围设备。不支持中心设备与外围设备之间的角色切换。广播和周期性物理链路提供从广播者到可能无限数量的扫描者或发起者的单向分组传输。

物理链路用作一条或多条支持异步业务的逻辑链路的传输载体。逻辑链路上的业务通过资源管理器中调度函数分配的物理链路被复用。

除了用户数据之外，链路层和物理层的控制协议也通过逻辑链路承载。这就是链路层协议（LL）。在微微网中处于活动状态的设备具有默认的 LE 异步连接逻辑传输（LE ACL），用于传输 LL 协议信令。默认 LE ACL 是在创建微微网时创建的逻辑传输。

链路层功能使用 LL 协议来控制微微网中设备的操作，并提供管理较低架构层（PHY 和 LL）的服务。

总体而言，微微网由活动物理链路上的一条 ACL 逻辑传输加上等时物理链路上的零条或多条 CIS 逻辑传输组成。此外，在信道探测物理链路上可能存在零个或多个临时信道探测过程。

与 BR/EDR 中一样，在链路层之上，L2CAP 层向应用和服务提供基于信道的抽象。它执行应用数据的分片和重组，以及在共享逻辑链路上对多个信道进行复用和分用。L2CAP 具有一个协议控制信道，在主 ACL 逻辑传输上承载。

除了 L2CAP 之外，LE 还提供了两个位于 L2CAP 之上的附加协议层。安全管理器协议（SMP）使用固定的 L2CAP 信道来实现设备之间的安全功能。另一个是属性协议（ATT），它提供了通过固定 L2CAP 信道通信少量数据的方法。设备还使用属性协议来确定其他设备的服务和能力。属性协议也可以在 BR/EDR 上使用。

LE 射频通过使用到达角（AoA）或出发角（AoD）方法提供检测另一 LE 射频相对方向的手段。

指 HCI 以下所有层的集合术语。

覆盖区域

两个蓝牙设备可以以可接受的质量和性能交换消息的区域。

安全连接创建

建立连接的过程，包括认证和加密。

可信关系创建

将远程设备标记为可信设备的过程。这包括为将来认证存储公共链路密钥，或者在链路密钥不可用时进行配对。

设备发现

从可发现设备检索蓝牙设备地址、时钟和设备类别的过程。

可发现设备

范围内周期性监听查询扫描物理信道并对该信道上的查询作出响应的 BR/EDR 设备。范围内以可连接或可扫描广播事件进行广播且广播数据中设置了可发现标志的 LE 设备。此设备处于可发现模式。

可发现模式

在 BR/EDR 中执行查询扫描或在 LE 中以设置了可发现标志的可发现或可连接广播事件进行广播的蓝牙设备。

发现过程

在 BR/EDR 中执行查询过程或在 LE 中使用设置了可发现标志的可发现或可连接广播事件扫描广播者的蓝牙设备。

HCI

主机控制器接口（HCI）提供到基带控制器和链路管理器的命令接口以及对硬件状态和控制寄存器的访问。此接口提供了访问蓝牙基带能力的统一方法。

主机

一个逻辑实体，定义为非核心配置文件以下、主机控制器接口（HCI）以上的所有层；即在 [卷 3](../host.html "Volume 3 Host")中规定的各层。连接到蓝牙控制器的蓝牙主机也可以与连接到各自控制器的其他蓝牙主机通信。

发起者

从广播承载的角度来看，在广播物理信道上监听可连接广播事件以形成连接的蓝牙低功耗设备。

从信道探测的角度来看，在信道探测步骤中首先发送的设备。

查询设备

正在执行查询过程的 BR/EDR 设备。此设备正在执行发现过程。

查询

蓝牙设备发送查询消息并监听响应以发现覆盖区域内其他蓝牙设备的过程。

查询扫描

蓝牙设备监听在其查询扫描物理信道上接收的查询消息的过程。

时刻

某事发生的某一时刻。具体而言，是指特定操作将发生的（BR/EDR）时隙或（LE）连接事件。

互操作性

两个或多个设备交换信息并使用已交换信息的能力。

等时数据

流中的信息，其中流中的每个信息实体受到与先前和后续实体的时间关系的约束。

已知设备

至少存储了 BD_ADDR 的蓝牙设备。

L2CAP

逻辑链路控制与适配协议

L2CAP 信道

两个设备之间在 L2CAP 层上服务于单个应用或高层协议的逻辑连接。

L2CAP 信道建立

在 L2CAP 层上建立逻辑连接的过程。

LE

蓝牙低功耗

LE 控制器

指 [卷 6](../low-energy-controller.html "Volume 6 Low Energy Controller")中定义的各层的术语。

链路

逻辑链路的简写。

链路建立

建立默认 ACL 链路以及设备之间链路和信道层次的过程。

链路密钥

两个设备所知并用于认证链路的密钥。

LMP 认证

用于验证远程设备身份的 LMP 层过程。

LMP 配对

认证两个设备并创建公共链路密钥的过程，该链路密钥可用作可信关系或（单一）安全连接的基础。

逻辑链路

用于向蓝牙系统客户端提供独立数据传输服务的最低架构层。

逻辑传输

不同逻辑链路之间共享的确认协议和链路标识符。

名称发现

检索可连接设备的用户友好名称（蓝牙设备名称）的过程。

分组

在物理信道上传输的聚合比特的格式。

寻呼

连接过程的初始阶段，其中设备发送一串寻呼消息，直到从目标设备接收到响应或发生超时。

寻呼扫描

设备监听在其寻呼扫描物理信道上接收的寻呼消息的过程。

寻呼设备

正在执行寻呼过程的蓝牙设备。

已配对设备

已创建链路密钥的蓝牙设备（在请求连接建立之前或在连接阶段期间创建）。

口令

在使用安全简单配对时用于认证连接的 6 位数字。

周期性广播同步信息

描述周期性广播的控制信息，蓝牙低功耗设备用以同步到其所描述的广播。

物理信道

以一个或多个设备对一系列射频载波的同步占用为特征。存在多种物理信道类型，其特性根据不同用途而定义。

物理链路

两个设备之间在基带或链路层级别的连接。

物理传输

使用一种或多种调制方案在射频信道上进行 PHY 分组传输和/或接收。

微微网

占用共享物理信道的设备集合（BR/EDR 中最多八台设备，LE 中恰好两台设备），其中一台设备是微微网中心设备，其余设备连接到它。

微微网中心设备

微微网中的 BR/EDR 设备，其蓝牙时钟和蓝牙设备地址用于定义微微网物理信道特性。

微微网中的 LE 设备，它发起微微网的创建，选择标识微微网的访问地址，并在每个连接事件中首先发送。

微微网外围设备

微微网中非微微网中心设备但连接到微微网中心设备的任何 BR/EDR 设备。

微微网中非中心设备但与其通信的 LE 设备。

PIN

在配对发生之前可用于认证到设备的连接的用户友好数字。

配置文件广播数据（PBD）

从无连接外围广播发送者向一个或多个

无连接外围广播接收者承载数据的逻辑链路。

伪噪声比特序列

随机生成的一系列比特。

反射者

在信道探测中，在信道探测步骤中响应发起者的发送而第二个发送的设备。

解析列表

用于生成和解析可解析私有地址的记录列表。每条记录包含本地身份解析密钥、对端身份解析密钥和对端身份地址。

往返时间

分组从发起设备传输到响应设备再返回发起设备所需的时间。

扫描者

在广播物理信道上监听广播事件的蓝牙低功耗设备。

散射网

具有一个或多个公共设备的两个或多个微微网。

服务发现

查询和浏览由另一蓝牙设备提供或通过另一蓝牙设备提供的服务的规程。

服务层协议

使用 L2CAP 信道传输 PDU 的协议。

静默设备

如果启用了蓝牙的设备不响应远程设备发出的查询，则它对远程设备表现为静默。

同步扫描物理信道

使外围设备能够从中心设备接收同步训练分组的物理信道。

同步训练

在一组固定频率上发送的一系列分组，提供足够的信息使接收设备开始接收相应的无连接外围广播分组，或在错过粗时钟调整后恢复当前的微微网时钟。

滴答
